text:
Because corn is normally established by direct seeding rather than transplanting, seed quality has an outsized effect on final stand and yield -- there is no opportunity to compensate for poor seed with a nursery stage. Farmers are advised to buy seed from a reliable, reputable source and, where practical, to check germination rate before planting a large area (for example using a simple roll-towel or moist-cloth germination test on a sample of seed).

An important caution specific to hybrid varieties (such as CP888, CP999, CP AAA, and 30B80 in the variety table): because hybrid seed is an F1 cross, seed saved from a hybrid crop and re-planted will segregate and lose the uniformity and vigour of the original hybrid. Farmers using hybrid varieties should buy fresh certified seed each planting rather than saving their own seed, unlike with the open-pollinated varieties (Leuang Mongkol, Sovanh 5, Samasathat, Sadai, Poat Domnoeb), where farmer-saved seed is a more viable option.
